original_card.question: Does the reported word-census parity-pruning error invalidate a specific exclusion we still rely on, and what bounded repair is justified?
methods: Independently reconstruct the tiny counterexample and trace one affected exclusion to its exact pruning code.
Compare corrected and unpruned enumeration on a small exhaustive domain, then audit the changed pruning implication.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Pin the old and proposed corrected engines, distinguish a disproved pruning rule from a disproved final bound, and state exactly which downstream exclusions need revalidation. #2973 is an author-checked source archive; neither its new f(7) claim nor all old conclusions are automatically accepted or rejected.

first_step.inspect: Read #2973 error description and MATH.md; manually reconstruct the prefix states of 01021323 before running any large census.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; no full enumeration or mathematical validation.

original_card.first_experiment: Reconstruct the eight prefix states of 01021323 and compare bit-0 versus Hamming-weight parity budgets independently. Trace the reported false prune to one pinned predecessor (#2542, #2634 or #2691), then test a small exhaustive domain. Stop after a source-impact handoff or corrected-prune proof; a full seven-label replay needs a separate resource budget and a named research decision it can change.
original_card.bottleneck_link: An unsound exclusion can wrongly close a mechanism; correcting its dependency boundary is more useful than extending the same census.
allowed_variations: One predecessor pruning rule, one independently exhaustive small domain, or one downstream dependency audit.
scope_change_triggers: Launching a larger census before validating the prune and explaining which active decision it changes.
Treating a small-domain counterexample to the old rule as a counterexample to every reported seven-label bound.

actual_scope: Decide whether the fixed L/2 firing set is monotone in length by proving the n=4 silence at lengths 14 and 16 and classifying the canonical firing sets through (5,16).
scope_change_reason: The eligible chronological handoff, after dropping the budget-blocked (7,18)/(7,20) census in comment 19021170 and the delivered child-rank bound, is comment 19022438 handoff 1. That handoff asks whether the firing set grows with L and names (4,14) and (5,16) as the next classification. Handoff 2 of the same comment is already #4148. The card forbids launching the seven-label census as this session's orientation, so that census stays open.
bottleneck_link: Side result on the prune's dependency boundary. A monotone extrapolation would mis-state which functionals still falsely prune on longer words. The n=4 collapse shows that growth through length 12 does not continue, without repairing a retained exclusion or changing the selected frontier.
stop_rule: Stop after the flat-excess proof for every 14-point and 16-point subset of F_2^4, the canonical censuses through (5,16), and the monotone comparison with the #3699/#3733 lengths. Do not run survey(7,18) or the n=5 length-18 census.
evidence: PROOF.md proves every 14-point subset of F_2^4 has excess at most 29 < base 35, and the full space has excess 42 < base 49. verify.py recomputes the flat maxima, matches the published per-mask tables at (4,8), (4,10), (4,12), (5,12) and (5,14), and classifies (4,14), (4,16) and (5,16). Firing-set sizes are 9,10,13,0,0 for n=4 and 24,25,25 for n=5. Witness 010201031213 fires for mask 1 at length 12 and the length-14 set is empty. Both excess routes agree. No seven-label census and no new kappa.
author: unpaidmoon
ai_assistance: Prepared by unpaidmoon with substantial Cursor Grok assistance for selection, the flat-excess argument, the census and the checks. No independent human or formal-kernel review claimed.

open_questions.question: For n=5, which even length first makes every functional sound for the fixed L/2 substitution?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Through length 16 the firing set is still exactly the 25 masks of weight at most 3. The n=4 collapse happened when the quadratic base overtook the 8-point flat cap. The 16-point level sets have not done that yet.
open_questions.first_step: Classify canonical words at (5,18) with this package's enumerator and compare the firing set with the weight-at-most-3 set.
open_questions.blocked_by: Length 16 already has 267890 canonical closed words. Length 18 was outside this session, and no general cap is proved.

open_questions.question: Which nonzero functionals falsely prune simple restored universal words at (7,18) and (7,20)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Comment 19021170 identifies that census as the domain that can change a maintained exclusion. This package deliberately does not run it.
open_questions.first_step: Budget a separate replay of survey(7,18) and survey(7,20) and compare firing functionals with the corrected weight-parity budgets.
open_questions.blocked_by: The seven-label state count. The card treats that replay as its own resource decision.

open_questions.question: Does any n>5 repeat the n=4 collapse one step after every low-weight mask has started firing?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The mechanism is the substituted budget overtaking a dimension-capped class excess. If it is special to n=4, the n=5 stability through length 16 should not be read as a law.
open_questions.first_step: Test one even length at n=6 past the first length whose firing set contains every mask of weight at most n-2.
open_questions.blocked_by: (6,16) already has 2262380 canonical closed words before the universality filter, and no threshold theorem is proved here.
